sources.note: A competitive chess testbed where 13 models play each other, and no model beats a human-amateur-level engine while some lose to random play.
sources.title: ChessArena: A Chess Testbed for Evaluating Strategic Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models

sources.note: A fully automated multi-turn reasoning benchmark of 40 tasks and 3600 instances requiring interaction with an environment, on which frontier reasoning models fall short.
sources.title: MTR-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multi-Turn Reasoning Evaluation

sources.note: Edits the internal representation of a written scratchpad state while holding the printed text fixed, and asks whether the next step follows the transition rule applied to the edited value — turning 'does the model use its scratchpad?' into a causal test with a single correct answer.
sources.title: Do Models Read What They Write? Causal Registers in Scratchpad Reasoning

sources.note: Gives the first optimization guarantee that gradient descent trains constant-depth transformers to solve NC1-complete problems with chain of thought, and shows the algebraic structure of the task decides how far the learned reasoning extrapolates.
sources.title: Transformers Provably Learn Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Length Generalization

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'state tracking'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:

- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.

result.definition: Maintaining an accurate representation of a changing situation across many steps, and across 4 sources a capability the archive evaluates as distinct from step-wise reasoning. Its benchmarks: a chess testbed where 13 models play each other and none beats a human-amateur-level engine while some lose to random play, and a multi-turn reasoning benchmark. Its mechanism is probed directly by the scratchpad work, which edits the internal representation of a written state while holding the printed text fixed and asks whether the next step follows the transition rule applied to the edited value -- a causal test with a single correct answer, whose move-specific selectivity gaps of +0.57 and +0.68 show the model combining the edited state with the supplied move. One theoretical source proves length generalisation for a procedure over states, which is the formal counterpart.
